subject: Black History Month Event Planning
overview: The Medford Human Rights Commission discussed upcoming community engagement initiatives for Black History Month and Martin Luther King Jr. Day, including an educational event at the Royal House and Slave Quarters. The commission also reviewed social media accounts, commission vacancy updates, and Open Meeting Law guidelines.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The commission approved the minutes from its previous meeting.

items.title: Black History Month and MLK Day Event Planning
items.summary: Commissioners agreed to organize a Black History Month event on February 11, 2023, at the Royal House and Slave Quarters focused on Belinda Sutton's 1783 petition, featuring youth service activities, music, and promotional materials. Member Kelly Cunha also presented an educational slideshow about Boston's 'The Embrace' sculpture to share with Medford Public Schools.

items.title: Website and Social Media Visibility
items.summary: The commission discussed municipal website updates and sharing existing Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn pages to improve public visibility.

items.title: Commission Vacancies
items.summary: Staff Liaison Frances Nwajei updated the commission on citywide vacancy announcements and plans to review candidate applications once more are received.

items.title: Public Comment and Open Meeting Law Discussion
items.summary: A member of the public asked about local MLK Day event dates, and commissioners discussed Open Meeting Law rules regarding quorum, subcommittees, and administrative communications between meetings.
